name: apprunner:UpdateService
description: A principal with apprunner:UpdateService can modify an existing App Runner service's configuration. If the target service has a privileged IAM role attached, the attacker can update the service to use the aws-cli image with a StartCommand that executes with the service role's permissions. Unlike creating a new service, this does not require iam:PassRole since the role is already attached to the existing service.
author: Seth Art

required.description: Target App Runner service ARN must be in the Resource section

additional.description: Check service configuration and confirm the attached role
Discover existing App Runner services to target

admin: An App Runner service must exist with an IAM role attached
The service's role must have administrative permissions
lateral: An App Runner service must exist with an IAM role attached

references.title: Getting Shell and Data Access in AWS App Runner

options.name: SERVICE_ARN
options.description: ARN of the existing App Runner service to update (must have a privileged role attached); auto-discovered when not set and a single service with a 'pl-' prefix exists in the region

options.name: TARGET_ARN
options.description: IAM user or role ARN to target (auto-resolved from caller identity if not set)

options.name: REGION
options.description: AWS region of the target App Runner service

options.name: CONTAINER_IMAGE
options.description: Container image to use for the exploit (aws-cli ENTRYPOINT; StartCommand becomes args)

options.name: CLEANUP
options.description: Restore the original App Runner service configuration after execution (starting user has apprunner:UpdateService so restoration is possible)

payloads.name: backdoor/attach-policy
payloads.description: Attach AdministratorAccess policy to an IAM user or role via App Runner service StartCommand
